title: Should in that-clauses; the present subjunctive
subtitle: They proposed that Felix (should) move to Munich.
summary: Report advice, orders and proposals with should in a that-clause, and use the more formal present subjunctive that drops should.

lesson.heading: that + should + bare infinitive
lesson.text: We can report advice, orders, requests and suggestions about things that need to be done with a that-clause containing **should** + bare infinitive. After *should* we often have *be* + past participle (passive) or *be* + adjective.

examples.text: They have proposed that Felix **should move** to their Munich office.
We advised that the company **should not raise** its prices.
They directed that the building **should be pulled** down.
We insist that the money **should be available** to all students in financial difficulties.

lesson.heading: The present subjunctive: leaving should out
lesson.text: In formal contexts, especially writing, we can drop *should* and use the **base form** of the verb - the present subjunctive. Other verbs used this way: advise, ask, beg, command, demand, insist, instruct, intend, order, prefer, recommend, request, require, stipulate, suggest, urge, warn.

examples.text: They have proposed that Felix **move** to their Munich office.
They directed that the building **be pulled** down.
We advised that the company **not raise** its prices.
examples.wrong: the company do not raise its prices

lesson.heading: Three levels of formality
rows: I suggested that he **should** give up golf.
I suggested that he **give** up golf.
I suggested that he **gives** up golf.

lesson.heading: After a reporting noun
lesson.text: The same that-clause with *should* or the subjunctive follows nouns related to those verbs - advice, order, proposal, warning, and so on.

examples.text: The police issued an **order** that all weapons (**should**) **be handed** in immediately.
The weather forecast gave a **warning** that people (**should**) **prepare** for heavy snow.

lesson.heading: it + be + adjective
lesson.text: After **it** + *be* + adjective we can use *should*, and sometimes the subjunctive. Also: advisable, appalling, appropriate, (in)conceivable, crucial, essential, imperative, important, obligatory, (un)necessary, urgent, vital.

examples.text: It is inappropriate that he **should receive** the award again.
It is imperative that we **should act** now to avoid war.
It is appalling that they **should be allowed** to go free.

lesson.heading: should for our own reaction
lesson.text: We also use **should** in a that-clause to comment on our own reaction to what we are reporting, especially after *be* + adjective. Also: amazed, amused, anxious, astounded, disappointed, shocked, surprised, upset.

examples.text: I am concerned that she **should think** I stole the money.
I am shocked that Kristina **should behave** so badly.
I am amused that he **should take** his appearance so seriously.

lesson.note: If you leave should out here, use an ordinary tense - not the subjunctive.

lesson.heading: Now, the future, and plans
lesson.text: **should** in a that-clause can describe a situation that exists now or one that may exist in the future. When we talk about an intention or a plan, the subjunctive is often available too.

examples.text: It's not surprising that they **should be** seen together - they're brothers.
We believe it is important that she **should take** the exam next year.
I've arranged that she **come** to the first part of the meeting.
examples.note: or ... that she should come ... / ... that she comes ... / ... for her to come ...

lesson.text: The subjunctive is only possible after verbs of advising, ordering and proposing. After *felt*, *reported*, *declared*, *agreed* or *announced*, *should* has to stay.

exercises.prompt: Lee said: 'Mara Bianchi would make an excellent export manager. Let's promote her.' -> Lee urged that Mara Bianchi ___ to export manager.
exercises.explanation: urge reports a proposal, so we use should + be + past participle.

exercises.prompt: Alice said: 'It would be valuable for us to send a sales representative to South Africa.' -> Alice recommended that a sales representative ___ to South Africa.
exercises.explanation: The action has still to be carried out, so should be sent is right.

exercises.prompt: Match each set of words with its report.

pairs.left: Simon said: 'It is vital to keep to our work schedules.'
pairs.right: Simon insisted that work schedules should be kept to.

pairs.left: Alina said: 'Perhaps we could use web conferencing to save money on air fares.'
pairs.right: Alina suggested that web conferencing should be used for meetings.

pairs.left: Alina said: 'Our head office must remain in London.'
pairs.right: Alina declared that the head office should remain in London.

pairs.left: Nathan said: 'It's okay for us to sponsor the European chess league.'
pairs.right: Nathan agreed that the company should sponsor the European chess league.

exercises.prompt: Complete the formal report: We advised that the company ___ its prices.
exercises.explanation: In the present subjunctive the negative is not + base form - never a form of do.

exercises.statement: They have proposed that Felix move to their Munich office.
exercises.explanation: Correct. propose allows the present subjunctive, so the base form move is right in formal writing.

exercises.statement: Lee felt that business in South America be expanded.
exercises.explanation: Lee felt that business in South America should be expanded. feel does not allow the subjunctive, so should must stay.

exercises.prompt: I am ___ that Kristina should behave so badly.
exercises.explanation: should + bare infinitive after be + adjective reports our reaction; behaving badly shocks us.

exercises.prompt: It is ___ that we should act now to avoid war.
exercises.explanation: it + be + adjective of necessity takes a that-clause with should.

exercises.prompt: Can should be left out of the that-clause (leaving the present subjunctive)?
It is ___ that they should be allowed to go free.
exercises.explanation: The speaker is outraged, so appalling fits; the that-clause keeps should.

exercises.prompt: Report the order the police gave. Put the words in order.
exercises.answer: The police issued an order that all weapons should be handed in immediately
alternatives: The police issued an order that all weapons be handed in immediately
exercises.explanation: A reporting noun like order takes the same that-clause with should (or the subjunctive be handed in).

exercises.prompt: Which version is the most formal?
options: I suggested that he give up golf.
I suggested that he should give up golf.
I suggested that he gives up golf.
exercises.explanation: The bare base form is the present subjunctive, the most formal of the three; gives up is the least formal.
